LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SUBJECT- VERB AGREEMENT

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we construct sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the subject and the verb in sentences
2. construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SUBJECT- VERB AGREEMENT
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SUBJECT- VERB AGREEMENT
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the subject and the verb in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the subject and the verb in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the subject and the verb in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the subject and the verb in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the subject and the verb in sentences)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement to a partner. (skill: construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the subject and the verb in sentences.
3. Practise this skill: construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we construct sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 14.3.1 Subject- Verb Agreement means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the subject and the verb in sentences.
5. Be able to: construct sentences ensuring subject-verb agreement.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
